correctness.rationale: Exact rank-one Chebyshev characteristic identity establishes the full eigenvalue equation for every even ring. Half-flux loss-free sine modes become simple zeros of the full dissipative polynomial; an implicit derivative gives -4i J^2 sin^2(theta)/(gamma n) times delta^2 plus analytic O(delta^4). Negative-imaginary-part argument excludes other slow modes. Continuous analytic spectral projections, orthonormality at exact half flux and antipodal weights 2/n yield the fixed-size rescaled norm limit. Midpoint Riemann quadrature yields exp(-tau/2)I_0(tau/2), with the standard Laplace tail. Seventy-seven finite-dimensional numerical checks replay; infinite theorem does not rely on enumeration.

originality.rationale: Historical-priority assessment is limited to examined evidence, not a uniqueness certification. Closest primary work (Krapivsky, Luck and Mallick, arXiv:1311.6298, section 4.2) analyzes the same local quantum trap on an unthreaded ring, but not the flux-detuned half-flux quasidark spectrum or Bessel survival scaling. Emary (arXiv:0705.2934, sections I-II) treats quadratic field lifting of dark current blockade in three-dot transport, but not the n-vertex single-trap survival law. The earlier exact flux-threaded static survival classification is explicitly outside this claim. Broad aliases, parameters, quantum-walk variants, and public indexed records were searched; no inspected stronger statement implies the mode-resolved coefficient or sequential survival limit.

value.rationale: The discontinuity between perfect half-flux protection and certain capture at nonresonant flux leaves a natural, physically decisive kinetic gap. This theorem resolves that gap with all n/2 quasidark spectral widths, an exact finite-size survival mixture, and a nontrivial sequential Bessel scaling whose algebraic tail contrasts with finite-ring exponential tails. Neither a static dark-space rank nor a generic current suppression supplies these observables.
